title.en: Current, potential difference and Ohm's law

text.en: Electric current flowing in a wire is like water flowing in a pipe. A battery supplies the push, called potential difference.

Electric current is the rate of flow of charge: I = Q/t. Its unit is the ampere (A), measured by an ammeter connected in series.
Conventional current flows from positive to negative terminal; electrons flow the other way.
Potential difference is the work done to move a unit charge: V = W/Q, in volts, measured by a voltmeter connected in parallel.
Ohm's law: at constant temperature, the current through a conductor is proportional to the potential difference, V = IR.
Resistance R is the property that opposes the flow of current. Its unit is the ohm.
Resistance R = rho x L / A. It increases with length, decreases with area of cross-section and depends on the material (resistivity rho).
Metals have low resistivity, alloys have higher resistivity and insulators very high. Nichrome is used in heaters.
A circuit diagram uses symbols for cell, switch, bulb, resistor, ammeter and voltmeter.
